summary: test-pipelines turns test output (JUnit XML) into stored, write-once results and computes mechanical verdicts, failure records and a scorecard from them. It plays the role of Chromium's ResultDB and LUCI Analysis, so every builder's results are kept and judged the same way.

how_it_works.title: The sink
how_it_works.text: A builder adds the sink action after its test steps. It normalizes every JUnit report into Result records, computes the run's verdict, and keeps the bundle (run.json, results.jsonl, verdict.json) as a workflow artifact. A job with no reports still stores a run marked as failing, because a missing signal is not a pass.

how_it_works.title: Only short messages are kept
how_it_works.text: Each stored Result keeps the first 20 lines and at most 1,000 characters of its failure or skip message, plus a short truncation marker, and never stores captured stdout or stderr. The full raw testcase is kept only with the opt-in keep-raw-junit flag, capped at 16,000 characters.

how_it_works.title: Store and scorecard
how_it_works.text: The scorecard workflow runs every six hours, collects qq-results artifacts from trusted workflow runs into the write-once results branch, and writes scorecard.md and scorecard.json. It reports gate time, main-red minutes, flake rate and pass rates, and lists unmeasured metrics instead of showing zero.

how_it_works.title: Retry, then compare with base
how_it_works.text: Given a rerun command, the sink reruns failed tests and then runs those still failing at the base commit. A test that passes on retry is FLAKY, one that fails the same way on base is EXONERATED, and anything else is UNEXPECTED and fails the change.

how_it_works.title: Failure records
how_it_works.text: Held canaries, canary rollbacks and auto-reverts each open one write-once Failure record mirrored to a labelled GitHub issue. Free text is withheld unless explicitly opted in, and records that look security-related are never mirrored to a public issue.

status.text: All four v0 items are merged: the result schema and sink, the store and scorecard, retry with base comparison, and failure records with issue mirrors.
Retry and base comparison only run when a builder passes a rerun command; this repo's own CI exercises them through tools/planted_demo.sh.

The exoneration rule is a heuristic that compares failure kinds and cannot tell two failures of the same kind apart. In a rebase-style queue with entries ahead, the base cannot be derived, so failures stay UNEXPECTED.
A ruleset blocking force-pushes and deletion on the results branch is still an open TODO.
